map.尺寸链/装配间隙分析中，用方和根（Root Sum Square）估算多个零件公: In dimension-chain / assembly-clearance analysis, use root-sum-square (Root Sum Square) to estimate the total variation after stacking multiple part tolerances, closer to statistical reality than worst case.
map.大批量生产下各零件误差近似独立随机分布，RSS 给出『典型』总公差而非极端值。: Under mass production each part's error is approximately an independent random distribution; RSS gives the 'typical' total tolerance rather than an extreme value.
map.在保证装配功能前提下，用 RSS 放宽容差以降本，而非一味按最坏情况加严。: On the premise of guaranteeing assembly function, use RSS to relax tolerances and reduce cost, rather than uniformly tightening per worst case.
map.总公差 T = √(t₁² + t₂² + … + tₙ²)，各 tᵢ 为各组成: Total tolerance T = √(t1² + t2² + … + tn²), each ti being each component-ring tolerance (take absolute value when stacking in the same direction). RSS assumes the errors are mutually independent and approximately normal, giving the typical total variation at about 99.73% (±3σ) confidence.
map.某装配尺寸链由三段组成，各段公差分别为 0.1、0.15、0.2 mm：T =: An assembly dimension chain consists of three segments with tolerances 0.1, 0.15, 0.2 mm respectively: T = √(0.1² + 0.15² + 0.2²) = √(0.01 + 0.0225 + 0.04) = √0.0725 ≈ 0.269 mm (RSS). Compared with the worst-case stacked 0.45 mm, RSS is significantly smaller, indicating that under mass production single-part tolerances can be appropriately relaxed without exceeding specs.
map.RSS 和最坏情况（WC）怎么选？: How to choose between RSS and worst case (WC)?
map.WC 假设所有误差同时取极值同向叠加，给出绝对安全但过严的总公差；RSS 假设独: WC assumes all errors simultaneously take extreme values stacked in the same direction, giving an absolutely safe but over-tight total tolerance; RSS assumes independent randomness and gives a typical value. Use WC for single-piece / small-batch / safety-critical parts, and RSS is more economical under mass-production statistical process control.
map.RSS 的前提是什么？: What is the premise of RSS?
map.要求各组成误差相互独立、且分布近似正态（或至少对称）；若存在系统性偏差（如刀具统: It requires each component error to be mutually independent and approximately normally distributed (or at least symmetric); if a systematic deviation exists (e.g. tools uniformly oversized), it should first be treated as a shift rather than random tolerance, otherwise RSS underestimates the true total error.
